## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

RecordedRaceSyncService — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/sync/RecordedRaceSyncService.kt

## Trigger

Receiving the phone's acknowledgement on `/recorded-race-ack`, carrying the race's identifier — nothing observes it

## Today

`RecordedRaceSyncService.sync` sends each race's payload via
`RecordedRaceTransport.send`, and the instant that call returns true it
calls `raceRepository.saveRecordedRace` then, on success,
`raceRecordingRepository.eraseRecorded(race.id)` — all in the same pass,
with no round trip to the phone in between. A successful `send` only
means the message left the watch (`WearableRecordedRaceTransport.send`
returns true once `MessageClient.sendMessage` completes to every
connected node); it says nothing about the phone having written the
race down. `RaceRecordingRepository.eraseRecorded`'s own doc comment
already states the intended contract — "called once the phone has
confirmed receipt" — but nothing in `sync` waits for such a
confirmation before calling it.

There is, in fact, no confirmation channel at all. No decoder exists
for the bytes `PayloadCodec` encodes (`core-sync/.../PayloadCodec.kt`:
"No decoder exists yet — no lot reads these bytes back"), and no
`WearableListenerService`/`MessageClient` listener exists anywhere in
`:app-phone` to receive a `/recorded-race` message. The `raceRepository`
that `RecordedRaceSyncService.sync` writes to is not the phone's
history: `:app-wear`'s own `SyncModule`/`RepositoryModule` wire
`RecordedRaceSyncService` with `:app-wear`'s own local `RaceRepository`
instance (its own `"hyrox-tracker.db"`), so today's "save" is a local,
in-process write on the watch, not a phone acknowledgement of anything.

## Expected

Once `transport.send` returns true, the watch marks that race as sent
and keeps it — `eraseRecorded` is not called at that point.
`RaceRecordingRepository` needs a way to record "sent, awaiting
acknowledgement" distinct from being erased, so a race already marked
sent is not resent as if it had never gone out. The watch erases a
race only when a message arrives on `/recorded-race-ack` carrying that
race's identifier, matched against the held race, and calls
`eraseRecorded` at that point instead. The phone sends that
acknowledgement only once it has actually saved the race, and sends it
again — without saving a second time — when it is acknowledging a race
whose identifier it already holds; the identifier alone is enough to
tell the two cases apart.

Building this needs more than a change to `RecordedRaceSyncService`:

- `RecordedRacePayload` carries no race identifier today (`name`,
  `date`, `segments`, `completion` only) — the phone has nothing to
  echo back in an acknowledgement, and nothing to compare against a
  race it already holds.
- No receiver exists on the phone for the Data Layer at all — no
  `WearableListenerService`/`MessageClient` listener in `:app-phone`
  decodes an incoming `/recorded-race` message, and `PayloadCodec` has
  no decoder, only `encode`. Today's "save" is `RecordedRaceSyncService`
  calling its injected `RaceRepository` directly, in-process, against
  the watch's own local database — never reaching the phone.
- No transport exists for a `/recorded-race-ack` message in either
  direction: nothing on the phone sends one, nothing on the watch
  listens for one.
- `RaceRepository.saveRecordedRace` has no identifier-based
  idempotency check — it always creates a fresh row (or `REPLACE`s a
  given non-zero id); nothing lets it recognise "I already hold a race
  with this identifier" so it can skip the write while an
  acknowledgement still goes out.
